summary: Fully verified the new ImageSourceDialog end-to-end: Add & Replace flows, Upload from PC (data URL) and Paste URL tabs, invalid-URL rejection, close via Cancel/X/backdrop, inside-click stopPropagation, Delete image, and backend PATCH accepting large base64 lists. All 5 backend pytest cases pass and all UI assertions pass.

issues: Pre-existing React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Caused by dynamic content in ProductDetail.jsx line 218 <option> children. Not related to this feature but should be cleaned up (interpolate as plain string).

action_items: (Optional/minor) Fix hydration warning in ProductDetail.jsx <option> children by using a template literal: `${c.group} · ${c.name}` — this is likely already the case; warning originates from an instrumented <span> wrapper. Safe to ignore for this feature.
critical_code_review_comments: ImageSourceDialog cleanly handles both modes; onSubmit awaited before onClose so errors keep the dialog open — good.
fileToResizedDataURL correctly clamps to maxDim 1600 and outputs JPEG q=0.85; PNG transparency loss is documented in the source.
proxyImg now bypasses /api/image-proxy for data: and blob: URLs — verified: uploaded images render directly from data URL, no proxy call.
Backend ProductUpdate.images: Optional[List[str]] accepts arbitrary strings incl. multi-MB base64 payloads (tested 1.5MB payload, 200 OK, GET-persisted).
Minor: dialog does not release object URL from URL.createObjectURL(file) on close — small memory leak per open; consider revokeObjectURL in cleanup.
seed_data_creation: Generated a tiny 2x2 PNG at /tmp/test_pixel.png for upload testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend uses in-memory AsyncMockDB and resets on backend restart, so any images added via tests won't persist across restarts. test_product_images.py picks the first product from GET /api/products for its subject; safe to re-run. UI test uses /tmp/test_pixel.png (2x2 PNG); regenerate if missing.
rca of the issue: N/A — all specified behaviors verified working.
